steps.premise: A first-timer may arrive without recognizing anyone.
steps.action: Have a host greet arrivals at the door and offer to accompany them to the lesson.
steps.consequence: The visitor has someone to go in with straight away.
steps.quote: Have a host meet people at the door and offer to walk them over to the lesson, sparing a first-time visitor the search for a familiar face.

steps.premise: A prospective guest might think a dance partner is required.
steps.action: Explicitly welcome solo guests in the invitation.
steps.consequence: People know in advance they can turn up on their own.
steps.quote: Say on the invitation that people can come alone so potential guests know they don't need to find a partner before they arrive.

steps.premise: Some beginners miss the first lesson or prefer to watch before trying.
steps.action: Give another short introduction later that evening.
steps.consequence: They still have an opportunity to learn how to start.
steps.quote: Repeat a brief introduction partway through the evening for someone who missed the opening lesson or needed a little time to watch.

steps.premise: Someone learning a figure may forget it mid-song.
steps.action: Teach a simple step that works for the length of a song.
steps.consequence: The beginner has a familiar movement to fall back on.
steps.quote: Give beginners a basic step they can use for a whole song, leaving them something dependable to return to when a new figure slips their mind.

steps.premise: Regulars may already be partnered when newcomers arrive together.
steps.action: Recruit a few regulars to volunteer to dance with first-timers.
steps.consequence: The new arrivals have experienced partners available.
steps.quote: Ask a few regulars to volunteer for dances with first-timers so an arriving group doesn't find all the experienced partners paired off.

steps.premise: New guests may be unsure how asking or turning down a dance will go.
steps.action: Act out a friendly invitation and a friendly refusal when welcoming the group.
steps.consequence: Guests hear what a comfortable exchange can sound like whichever answer is given.
steps.quote: Model both a friendly invitation and a friendly decline during the welcome. Guests get to hear how either answer can end comfortably.

steps.premise: Some pairs feel more secure learning together.
steps.action: Let each pair decide whether to rotate partners during the lesson.
steps.consequence: Those who prefer their original partner can continue practicing together.
steps.quote: Make partner changes optional during the lesson so two people who feel steadier practicing together can keep their place.

steps.premise: A learner needs to understand the parts in a partner dance to choose one.
steps.action: Explain what each partner does, then let each learner pick a role.
steps.consequence: People can study the part they want.
steps.quote: Teach partner roles by describing what each person does and let people choose which part they want to learn.

steps.premise: Someone who pauses for breath may need a gentler tempo to come back.
steps.action: Play slower music at intervals throughout the evening.
steps.consequence: A dancer who has rested can rejoin at a pace they can handle.
steps.quote: Mix slower tracks into the program throughout the night, giving someone catching their breath a chance to rejoin at a manageable pace.

steps.premise: A beginner may want to know which dance is next before standing up.
steps.action: Name the dance before starting the track.
steps.consequence: The beginner has time to choose whether to take the floor.
steps.quote: Announce the type of dance before the music starts so a beginner has time to decide whether to get up for it.

steps.premise: Crowd movement can interrupt a beginner repeating a step.
steps.action: Keep practice space open just off the main dance floor.
steps.consequence: Learners can try a movement several times at their own pace.
steps.quote: Leave a little room beside the main floor for people to try a step a few times without being swept along by the crowd.

steps.premise: Spinning may be uncomfortable for some dancers.
steps.action: Demonstrate a simpler turn with both feet staying near the floor.
steps.consequence: They can still dance that part of the figure.
steps.quote: Show an easy version of a turn that keeps both feet close to the floor, giving anyone who finds spinning uncomfortable a way through the figure.

steps.premise: A pair that loses the beat might otherwise sit out the remainder.
steps.action: Teach partners to pause and find the beat again.
steps.consequence: They can resume dancing during the same song.
steps.quote: Teach a pair how to stop and pick up the beat again. Losing time needn't cost them the rest of the song.

steps.premise: A beginner may want a social dance without coaching.
steps.action: Ask regulars to get their partner's agreement before offering advice.
steps.consequence: The beginner decides whether to receive tips while dancing.
steps.quote: Ask regulars to check whether a partner wants feedback before giving tips, letting a beginner enjoy a dance without an unexpected lesson.

steps.premise: A guest may sit out a song and still want to be part of the social.
steps.action: Arrange the seats so the dancing is visible.
steps.consequence: Following the action from a chair can feel like taking part.
steps.quote: Set out chairs with a view of the floor so watching a song feels like participating in the evening and offers a chance to see the steps.

steps.premise: Sitting out can provide time to learn by watching.
steps.action: Give seated guests a clear view of the dancers.
steps.consequence: They can see how the steps are done.
steps.quote: Set out chairs with a view of the floor so watching a song feels like participating in the evening and offers a chance to see the steps.

steps.premise: A new dancer taking a water break may be unfamiliar with the room.
steps.action: Put water where guests can readily see and reach it.
steps.consequence: They can get a drink without searching for the host.
steps.quote: Put drinking water somewhere easy to spot and reach, allowing a new dancer to take a break without having to track down the host.

steps.premise: On a crowded floor a new couple may be unsure where others will pass.
steps.action: Show the whole group which direction dancers move in.
steps.consequence: Beginners can anticipate the traffic around them.
steps.quote: Walk everyone through the direction of travel on a busy floor so a new couple knows where other dancers are likely to pass.

steps.premise: Working on unfamiliar steps already takes a guest's attention.
steps.action: Give coats and bags a place outside the dancing area.
steps.consequence: Dancers can move through the floor without dodging people's things.
steps.quote: Give bags and coats a home away from the dancing area. A guest concentrating on unfamiliar steps shouldn't have to weave around belongings.

steps.premise: Noise can make a demonstration hard to follow by ear.
steps.action: Illuminate the instructor's face and feet during demonstrations.
steps.consequence: Learners can follow visible cues.
steps.quote: Keep the teacher's face and feet well lit during demonstrations so people can use visual cues when the room is noisy.

steps.premise: A newcomer may face a partner who repeatedly asks them to dance.
steps.action: Identify by name the host who handles that situation.
steps.consequence: Newcomers know whom to approach for help.
steps.quote: Point out a named host who can help if a partner keeps pressing for a dance, giving newcomers someone specific to approach.

steps.premise: Guests may hesitate to try new movements if pictures could appear online.
steps.action: Explain the photography arrangements and take group photos with people who agree to take part.
steps.consequence: Guests can practice without worrying about turning up in a post.
steps.quote: Make the photo arrangement clear and take group pictures with willing participants so people can try unfamiliar movements without worrying about appearing in a post.

steps.premise: Arrivals need to know how much to pay and what the door accepts.
steps.action: List the door charge and accepted payment methods in the invitation.
steps.consequence: Guests can bring the right payment and go straight in to meet the host.
steps.quote: Include the door price and payment options in the invitation so people can arrive with the fare in hand and head straight in to meet the host.

steps.premise: People who sit out several dances may still want to meet others.
steps.action: Turn the music down during a break and invite a short conversation.
steps.consequence: They can get acquainted with the group while off the floor.
steps.quote: Invite people to chat briefly over a break with the music turned down. Someone who sat out a few songs can still get to know the group.

steps.premise: People may be too shy to ask a question during the lesson.
steps.action: Put an anonymous question box by the exit.
steps.consequence: They can leave a question without speaking in front of the class.
steps.quote: Leave an anonymous question box by the exit and use the questions to shape the next introduction, reaching people who felt too shy to speak up in class.

steps.premise: The questions left by quiet learners show what they wanted to ask.
steps.action: Use the submitted questions when planning the next introduction.
steps.consequence: The next lesson can address concerns that went unspoken during class.
steps.quote: Leave an anonymous question box by the exit and use the questions to shape the next introduction, reaching people who felt too shy to speak up in class.
